scenarios.title: Big Slick at a short table
scenarios.prompt: The small blind shoves and the action returns to you in the big blind. Against the shown 22–QQ, AJs+, AQo+ range, what is your decision?
scenarios.actionReason: Calling needs 40% equity. AKo has about 46% against the stated range, making the call profitable in chip EV.
scenarios.mathPrompt: What equity percentage is required to call 1,800 into a final pot of 4,500?

scenarios.title: Button pressure
scenarios.prompt: It folds to you on the button with 11 big blinds. The blinds fold often enough that a shove is profitable. Choose your action.
scenarios.actionReason: A5 suited combines an ace blocker with usable equity when called. At 11bb, the modeled shove gains more than a small raise or fold.
scenarios.mathPrompt: Ignoring showdown equity for this sub-calculation, what fold percentage would a risk of 11,000 need to win the current 2,625 pot?

scenarios.title: Set-mining price
scenarios.prompt: A tight early-position player opens to 800 and you close the action in the big blind. The opener has 14,400 behind. Choose your action.
scenarios.actionReason: The direct price plus deep effective stacks support a call. The scenario assumes the tight opener can pay enough often when you flop a set.
scenarios.mathPrompt: Using the practical 12-to-1 set-mining guideline, how many additional chips beyond the current 1,700 final pot must you expect to win to justify the 600 call?
scenarios.mathExplanation: A 12-to-1 target requires about 7,200 in total return for a 600 call. The immediate final pot is 1,700, leaving roughly 5,500 to win later.

scenarios.title: Two cards guaranteed
scenarios.prompt: Your opponent is all-in, so a call guarantees both turn and river. Treat the nine remaining hearts as clean outs. Choose your action.
scenarios.actionReason: The nut-flush draw arrives by the river about 35% of the time, comfortably above the 25% call threshold.
scenarios.mathPrompt: Approximately how often will nine clean outs hit by the river from the flop?

scenarios.title: Not every straight card is clean
scenarios.prompt: You face a large flop bet. The range model discounts the two heart straight-completing cards because they also complete a flush draw. Choose your action.
scenarios.actionReason: Eight nominal straight outs become roughly six clean-equivalent outs after discounting the heart cards. The large price and future-street risk make folding best.
scenarios.mathPrompt: You have eight nominal open-ended straight outs. If both heart outs count as half-outs, how many clean-equivalent outs do you have?
scenarios.mathExplanation: Six fully clean outs plus two half-outs equals seven clean-equivalent outs.

scenarios.title: Defending against two-thirds pot
scenarios.prompt: The preflop raiser bets two-thirds pot. Q-high with little backdoor equity sits near the bottom of your range. Choose your action.
scenarios.actionReason: A range may need to continue often, but this specific low-equity combination is an appropriate fold within that range.
scenarios.mathPrompt: Against a 3,000 bet into 4,500, what is the theoretical minimum defense frequency?

scenarios.title: A genuinely close turn
scenarios.prompt: You face a small turn bet with the nut-flush draw plus a gutshot. Under the stated range model, call and fold are nearly tied. Choose your action.
scenarios.actionReason: The price is close to your discounted equity. Calling is slightly higher EV, but folding is within the scenario's numerical-equivalence band.
scenarios.mathPrompt: Using nine clean flush outs only, what is your approximate chance to hit on the river?
scenarios.mathExplanation: There are 46 unseen cards on the turn: 9 / 46 = 19.57%, close to the Rule of 2 estimate.

scenarios.title: Low-SPR overpair
scenarios.prompt: The turn is checked to you with an overpair and only 6,000 effective behind. Choose the modeled value action.
scenarios.actionReason: The effective SPR is only 0.6. Against the stated top-pair-heavy continuing range, moving all-in captures more value than checking.
scenarios.mathPrompt: What is the effective stack-to-pot ratio with 6,000 behind and a 10,000 pot?

scenarios.title: Semi-bluff ledger
scenarios.prompt: Your opponent checks. The model estimates a 6,000 semi-bluff succeeds immediately 45% of the time and retains draw equity when called. Choose your action.
scenarios.actionReason: The immediate fold component alone is close to break-even, and the flush equity when called pushes the 6,000 bet into positive EV.
scenarios.mathPrompt: Ignoring draw equity for this sub-calculation, what is the immediate-fold EV of betting 6,000 into 8,000 if Villain folds 45%?

scenarios.title: River bluff-catcher
scenarios.prompt: You face a one-third-pot river bet. Range analysis estimates Villain is bluffing 30% of the time. Choose your action.
scenarios.actionReason: Calling needs 25% wins and the stated range bluffs 30%, so the bluff-catch is profitable.
scenarios.mathPrompt: What equity is required to call 2,000 when the pot before your call is 6,000?

scenarios.title: The ace blocker bluff
scenarios.prompt: Villain checks the river. Your missed draw holds the ace of hearts, removing nut-flush combinations from Villain's range. The model chooses a half-pot bluff.
scenarios.actionReason: The blocker improves the composition of Villain's remaining range, and the modeled fold frequency exceeds the half-pot bluff threshold.
scenarios.mathPrompt: What fold percentage makes a 6,000 pure bluff into a 12,000 pot break even?

scenarios.title: Bubble risk premium
scenarios.prompt: One player is one blind from elimination on a satellite bubble. The ICM model requires 48% equity for this call, while your range equity is 44%. Choose your action.
scenarios.actionReason: The call may be acceptable in chip EV, but the satellite payout and short stack create a large risk premium. Forty-four percent is below the modeled 48% ICM threshold.
scenarios.mathPrompt: The chip-EV call threshold is 38.89%, while the ICM threshold is 48%. How many percentage points of risk premium does ICM add?
scenarios.mathExplanation: Risk premium here is 48% - 38.89% = 9.11 percentage points.
